steps.title: Documents (web) — upload, category, audience, schedule, delete; announcements attach a document
steps.goal: Every active member sees a Documents entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/documents`, the documents published to an audience they belong to, filterable by category, with Open (PDF, images) or Download (Word, Excel, text) buttons on one-hour signed URLs. A `documents.upload` holder uploads files up to 50 MB from the eight-type allow-list with title, category, audience group and publish time (now or scheduled), edits that metadata, resumes or discards incomplete uploads, and deletes documents (objects removed by the cron drain). Announcement managers attach a published document to an announcement through a real picker (replacing 3.5a's disabled placeholder) with an audience-mismatch warning, and announcement lists show a paper-clip link. `@church/db` gains `queries/documents.ts` (deferred by 1.7a). Documents never push — `notification_kind` has no `document` value — and the UI says so.

## Goal
When you finish, every active member of a church sees a **Documents** entry in the org navigation and, at `/o/<slug>/documents`, the documents published to an audience they belong to, filterable by category, with an Open button (PDF and images open in a new tab) or a Download button (Word, Excel and text files, which browsers cannot render) backed by one-hour signed URLs. A leader holding `documents.upload` can upload a file of up to 50 MB from the allow-list (PDF, JPG, PNG, TXT, Word, Excel) with a title, an optional category, an audience group and a publish time (now or scheduled), edit that metadata later, resume or discard an incomplete upload, and delete a document (the object is removed by the cron drain). Announcement managers can attach a published document to an announcement: 3.5a's disabled "Attach a document" placeholder becomes a real picker and the announcement lists show a paper-clip link that opens the document. Documents never send a push on their own — `notification_kind` has no `document` value — so the form says so and points at "create an announcement and attach this document". The mobile app is untouched (5.4b).

## Build

Export the module from `packages/db/src/index.ts` and fix the README line that said documents were deferred.

Export from `packages/domain/src/index.ts`.
3. **Form schema** `apps/web/src/features/documents/form-schema.ts`: `documentUploadFormSchema` = `{ title 1–160, description optional ≤ 4000 (only if the column exists), category optional (documentCategorySchema), audience_group_id uuid (required in the UI — store the `everyone` system group for "All attendees", never null, as 3.5a does), publish_mode: 'now' | 'schedule', publish_at_local (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`, required when 'schedule'), file_name, mime_type ∈ BUCKETS.documents.allowedMimeTypes, file_size_bytes ≤ effective cap }` with the message "Documents can be PDF, JPG, PNG, TXT, Word or Excel files up to 50 MB"; `documentEditFormSchema` = the metadata subset plus `publish_mode`/`publish_at_local`; `toDocumentInput(form, tz, now)` producing what `documentSchema` accepts; `resolveDocumentMime(fileName: string, reportedType: string): { ext, mime } | null` — pure, string arguments so the Server Action re-runs it (mirror `resolveBulletinMime`): trust `reportedType` when non-empty and `isAllowedMime('documents', reportedType)`, else map the lowercase extension (`pdf`, `jpg`/`jpeg`, `png`, `txt`, `doc`, `docx`, `xls`, `xlsx`) to its canonical MIME, else `null`; `ext = extensionForMime(mime)`. Documents have no push: `notification_kind` is `announcement, event, survey, bulletin` and `app.on_content_publish` is not attached to `documents`. 5.4a/5.4b treat 'create an announcement and attach the document' as the notify path and say so in the UI and docs. If the founder wants a push on document publish, that is an enum addition (`9998a_enum.sql` / `9998b_use.sql` pattern) plus a trigger, a mobile preference switch and a `notificationTargetPath('document', id)` — a new step, not 5.4.

System audience groups are protected only in the UI and Server Actions: DESIGN §6 grants the manager pair update/delete on every `audience_groups` row, and nothing in `9999_init.sql` forbids renaming or deleting the six system rows (which would break `SYSTEM_AUDIENCE_GROUPS` name parity and `app.on_org_created` assumptions). Recommend G2/G3 add a trigger `app.guard_system_audience_groups` (before update of name/kind/description-or-delete on rows with `kind <> 'custom'` → raise) plus an RLS test while `9999_init.sql` is unfrozen; otherwise 5.6's `9998_join_codes.sql` or a `9998_*` sibling should carry it. 5.5 does not add a migration.

Deleting a custom group sets `audience_group_id` to null on announcements/documents/calendars (G2's FK choice) and `app.user_in_group(null)` is true, so targeted content silently becomes visible to everyone. 5.5 mitigates with a consequences dialog (counts from `countGroupUsage`) and verifies the FK actions via `pg_constraint`. If the orchestrator prefers a safer default (e.g. re-point to the `everyone` system row, or `restrict`), that is a G2 schema change plus a change to 5.5's Build 7 copy. The FK action on `notifications.audience_group_id` is not stated in PLAN/DESIGN; 5.5 tells the agent to read it.

No member-count for system groups and no 'preview recipients' anywhere: computing `youth`/`men`/`women` client-side needs birthdates that `directory_persons` masks for managers who are not directory admins. A client RPC such as `count_audience_group(group_id)` (security definer, returns an integer only) would let 5.5's page and the announcement form show 'reaches N people / M with push' — it needs a migration and grants, so it is a candidate follow-up step (Phase 2 hardening 5.7 or a new 5.8), not part of 5.5.

Whether `directory_persons` exposes `user_id` (needed for the 'No account — will not receive pushes' badge) is not stated in PLAN/DESIGN; 5.5 makes the badge conditional on the view. G2/G3 could expose a boolean `has_account` at admin level if the founder wants the badge guaranteed.
